newsitem.title: USA: PRODI SAYS CLINTON MADE "BIG MISTAKE" ON NATO/RPT.
newsitem.headline: PRODI SAYS CLINTON MADE "BIG MISTAKE" ON NATO/RPT.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi told U.S. President Bill Clinton on Saturday he had made a "big mistake" by excluding Romania and Slovenia from the first round of NATO enlargement.
Prodi told a news conference at the Group of Seven summit that the two nations should be allowed in to help stabilise NATO's volatile southeastern flank.
The United States surprised its allies last week by saying that only three former Warsaw Pact states -- the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland -- should be included in the first wave of new members.
"There is a complete difference of opinion on this matter," Prodi said. "I said Mr. President, this is a big mistake."
Prodi said Italy had a strong interest in seeing NATO expand southwards because of Rome's involvement in the Balkans.
Italy leads a 6,000-strong multinational peace-keeping force in Albania.

"We live in one of the most difficult areas of the world," said Prodi. "We think that a balanced NATO expansion in the south is in our interest. It is in the interest of Italy and for peace in the area."

NATO will meet in Madrid on July 8 to formally decide which former communist countries to invite to apply for membership. Despite strong support from France and Italy, Romania and Slovenia are unlikely to overcome U.S. opposition. REUTER
